summary: On the starting code, only 4 of 20 journey runs passed, all of them gift lists. A new relative lost their invite at sign-up, guests could not open shared links, wishlists had no menu entry, and the exchange page ran off the side of phones. On the final commit, all 20 runs pass at 1440px and 390px in both themes. One privacy fix is live in production. Everything else is on the ux-audit branch and not deployed.
verified: Journeys: 20 of 20 runs pass on commit b6543b5, up from 4 of 20 on the starting code. That covers 1440px and 390px in Festive and Apple. Retries were allowed once and no journey needed one.

Accessibility: axe found serious or critical problems on 15 routes before and none after, in every journey run on the final commit. A separate sweep of 20 routes ran 124 audits per project on 918d766.
Keyboard: the keyboard-only passes of journeys 2 and 5 pass in both themes.
Unhappy paths: 15 of 16 checks pass in all four runs. The one failure is refreshing a half-filled form, which is logged under Your calls.
The draw: 1,000 random groups and exclusions, plus up to 100 redraws, checked against a brute-force oracle. Nobody drew themselves, everyone gave and received once, and every exclusion held.
Secrecy: in every Journey 2 run, no API response any participant's browser received, and no post-draw email, revealed who drew them.
Email: all 15 email types reached local Mailpit through real SMTP, each with text and HTML parts and correct links. Every address was @example.com, and no real email was sent.
Database: Journey 2 confirms the saved draw is valid, and no background job failed.
Test suites on b6543b5: bin/local-preview e2e passed 6 of 6, Rails passed 620 runs with 0 failures, and npm test passed 7 of 7 tasks including 292 web tests.
Dashboard date fix: confirmed in a real browser. A Christmas list started from Home now reads Friday, December 25, 2026, with 56 days to the deadline.
Production: the privacy fix deployed as f6fb256. The API and web services report that image, the deploy smoke tests passed, and health checks return 200.
limits: Everything except the privacy fix is undeployed. The Match screen data-loss fix is on this branch and not in production.

The privacy fix was not checked against a real shared wishlist in production, because that means touching production data. The proof is the test, which fails on the old code, plus the deployed version.
Real email delivery was not tested. Mail stopped at Mailpit by instruction, so Postmark, spam placement and real inboxes are unverified.
Apple, Google, Facebook and LinkedIn sign-in were not tested. Only email codes were.
Clerk's human check is bypassed in test mode, so what a real relative sees at that step is unknown.
Phone means Chromium at 390px with touch emulation. No real iPhone, iOS Safari or Android device was used.
Time in the scoreboard is robot time on a local dev server, so it says nothing about real load speed or real people.
Intermittent: about 1 in 14 phone runs had an automated tap land on the wrong element. It didn't happen in the final run and the cause is unknown.

Intermittent: Clerk's sign-in form hung in some repro runs after accepting a code. The server reported success, and Clerk's dev API was failing requests at the time. Reload recovery couldn't be tested, and I don't know whether production is affected.
Axe can't score text on gradients and left thousands of nodes incomplete. Gradient stops were checked by calculation. Sampled items looked like false positives, but not all of them were reviewed.
Error pages were never rendered in an axe run, and /settings was audited in its default section only.
Known gaps left open: two quick picks in the Match dialog can overlap and the last save wins. Manage Group can't be opened by keyboard. The MCP share_holiday tool replaces the link on every call.

The first baseline had script mistakes on Festive and phones. Those journeys were fixed and rerun on the frozen starting code, so the before numbers are fair. The baseline also includes the local Clerk redirect setting, to match production.

Competitor research: Reddit refused automated reading, Google Play coverage was thin, and mention counts show how often something came up, not how common it is. Status notes on the feature list come from reading code.
GitHub reports 28 dependency vulnerabilities on the default branch, 1 of them critical. They were outside this audit and were not reviewed.
The fresh agent ran on 149d47a, before the dashboard date fix, and its no-code rule was an instruction, not a technical block. It isn't a real person, so run the hallway test too.
Disk space ran out during testing and crashed Docker once. It only interrupted the fresh agent's run, and no final results came from that session.

fresh.intro: A fresh agent acted as a first-time user. It had no knowledge of this audit and could only look at pages, click, type and read its email. It was told not to read any code, though nothing technically prevented it. It passed all five tasks on commit 149d47a, before the dashboard date fix. A full disk on the test machine interrupted it during Task 2. That wasn't a site bug, and the agent resumed where it stopped.

tasks.name: Manage gift lists
tasks.note: Finished. The first gift took 2 tries, because the test tool hit the Next.js dev badge.

tasks.name: Run an exchange
tasks.note: Five sessions joined from real emails. Nobody drew themselves, the couple's rule held, and Olivia could not find who drew her.

tasks.name: Log in and out
tasks.note: Five presses of Back all landed on sign-in, and nothing private showed.

tasks.name: Navigate
tasks.note: Found everything from the menu, and the /oops page explained itself.

tasks.name: Wishlist
tasks.note: A guest on a phone reserved an item with no account, and the owner saw no spoiler.

stumbles: Annoying: the Christmas list said Deadline: Today. This is now fixed.
Annoying: Save & Add Another kept Maya, so Dad's gift went to both of them.
Annoying: marking a gift Purchased left Progress at 0% complete.
Annoying: the page says Draw names, but the button says Publish Exchange, which sounded like making it public.
Annoying: the invite knew Nana's email, but sign-up was empty, so Nana typed everything on a phone.
Annoying: Home never mentions the exchange, and Dec 25 isn't in Upcoming Dates.
Annoying: Settings opens with an MCP OAuth URL above the profile.
Possibly the test browser: Copy link said Failed to copy link. The scripted journeys copied successfully.
Minor: nothing shows that a gift name can be clicked to edit it, and the box stayed open after pressing Enter on a rename, though it had saved.
Minor: the Who is it for? dropdown stays open and covers the Status buttons.
Minor: the Recipients card shows a warning triangle beside Ready, and the 10 free gifts limit was a surprise.
Minor: Sign In or Sign Up is a guess for an invited relative.
Minor: Exclusion Rules has no add button until a second person is added, and 1 joined so far sits above five names.
Minor: your match appears on the page right after the draw, with no reveal step, so anyone nearby can see it.
Minor: the anonymous ask for ideas sends on one tap, with no confirmation.
Minor: the phone header takes a big chunk of the screen, and exchange relatives never appear in People.
Minor: there's no signed-out message, the 404 page has no main menu, and the menu says Options while the page says Settings.
Minor: the cousin's claim button is a small gift icon with no word.
Confusing overall: the F-key labels, Workspace for one person, Set Visible Status, what Match does, and Enter Start free.
Liked: the retro look, two-step gift adding, near-effortless exchange setup, the invite email's voice, returning to the invite after sign-up, and You're in. Waiting for Olivia to draw names.
